reason: Aurelius Systems is a ~15-person, $10M-seed San Francisco defense startup whose live Director of Engineering posting asks for someone to 'drive the hard handoff from a thing that works in the lab to a thing that survives downrange' - a verbatim restatement of Barry Hess's lab-to-field / prototype-to-fielding niche, and its live Lead, Mission Operations posting names the warfighter-to-build-team bridge that is his advocacy-chain offer.

company.name: Aurelius Systems, Inc.
company.one_liner: VC-backed defense startup building Archimedes, an autonomous edge-deployed directed-energy laser turret that detects, tracks and destroys Group 1/2 drones for counter-UAS.
company.industry: Defense technology / directed energy / counter-UAS hardware + AI autonomy
company.stage: Seed - $10M closed 2025-09-03, co-led by General Catalyst and Draper Associates (Outlander, Squadra, Decisive Point, Detroit Venture Partners, Alumni Ventures, GoAhead, New Founding, EO Tech, Mana); ~10-15 employees; founded 2024; DIU and USSOCOM listed among backers on their own site
company.hq: San Francisco, CA (R&D lab) with a Detroit manufacturing hub and a 400-acre private test range

evidence_jobs.title: Director of Engineering
evidence_jobs.quote: We need an Engineering Director to own the path from R&D to production across the whole system... drive the hard handoff from a thing that works in the lab to a thing that survives downrange and gets built at volume.

evidence_jobs.title: Lead, Mission Operations
evidence_jobs.quote: We need a field-first mission operations leader to be the company's primary bridge between the warfighter and the build team. This is a foundational MOPs role and a player-coach seat for the first 6 to 12 months, you'll build the function from scratch and run it yourself before you scale it.

people_spec: CEO & Co-Founder (Michael LaFramboise) - owns the transition-to-program-of-record problem and the runway clock; primary target
CTO & Co-Founder (John Marmaduke) - owns the lab-to-downrange engineering handoff the Director of Engineering req describes; secondary target
Head of Ops (title referenced in their own Operations Specialist posting; name not public) - owns build-floor and field-test logistics

NOTE: there is no VP Engineering or Director of Engineering to contact - that seat is the open req. There is also no cleared, DoD-acquisition-side senior leader visible anywhere in the company; that absence is the opening.
talk_track: Michael - I ran engineering at a DoD small business for sixteen years and put a tactical app platform into operators' hands in theater; it got adopted downrange and still never went force-wide, because nobody senior inside the building owned it. Your Director of Engineering posting asks for someone to "drive the hard handoff from a thing that works in the lab to a thing that survives downrange and gets built at volume." That req covers one half of the handoff. The other half is the part no engineering hire can do: converting the one- and two-stars who watch Archimedes drop a drone at your demos into an advocacy chain that reaches the program office writing the transition money. Field enthusiasm doesn't become a program of record on its own, and the clock on that conversion is your funded runway, not your hardware. Who inside the building would sponsor Archimedes today?
